---
title: "Tasks"
---

A CodeBook Lab task is a folder with exactly two files, named exactly as shown:

- `codebook.json`: the annotation scheme exported from CodeBook Studio
- `ground-truth.csv`: the texts, with the human labels filled in

For example:

```text
my_tasks/
  policy-sentiment/
    codebook.json
    ground-truth.csv
```

## Codebook Fields

The codebook names the column that holds the text and defines the questions, grouped into sections:

```json
{
  "header_column": "title",
  "text_column": "text",
  "metadata_columns": ["speaker", "source"],
  "section_1": {
    "section_name": "Policy Sentiment",
    "section_instruction": "Read the short text and assess whether it expresses an evaluative stance.",
    "annotations": {
      "annotation_1": {
        "name": "Direction",
        "type": "dropdown",
        "options": ["positive", "negative", "mixed", "no clear sentiment"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The top-level keys do different jobs in Studio and Lab:

`text_column`
: The column with the text to annotate. This is the only column the model sees: each prompt contains the codebook instructions and this text, nothing else from the row.

`header_column`
: A short title Studio shows above each text. Lab ignores it.

`metadata_columns`
: Optional columns Studio shows to coders for context. Lab ignores this list too. Every non-label column in your CSV, listed here or not, is copied to the model's output file unchanged, but none of them are sent to the model.

Sections are the keys that start with `section_`, and Lab processes them in order. Within a section, questions are ordered by the number at the end of their key (`annotation_1`, `annotation_2`, …), the same order Studio shows them in. This order matters for [conditional questions](conditionals-retries.qmd#conditional-annotations) and, in the default chat mode, for what the model has already answered about a text when it reaches each question.

Each question's column is named `<section name>_<question name>`. In this example the column is `Policy Sentiment_Direction`. Names are matched exactly, including spaces and capitalisation. If you rename a section or question in Studio after annotating, export the labels again so the column names in `ground-truth.csv` match the codebook.

## Ground Truth CSV

The CSV should include the source text column named by `text_column`, plus the human annotation columns implied by the codebook.

```csv
doc_id,title,text,Policy Sentiment_Direction
ps_001,Carbon Border Reform,The reform is a sensible compromise.,positive
ps_002,Housing Plan Criticism,The plan has an admirable goal but unrealistic financing.,negative
```

When Lab runs annotation, it drops the human label columns before prompting the model, so the model never sees the answers it will be scored against.

Lab matches each model answer to its human label **by row position**, not by an ID column: row 1 of the output is scored against row 1 of `ground-truth.csv`, and so on. Lab keeps rows in their original order, so this works as long as you don't sort, filter or edit `ground-truth.csv` between running and scoring. A stable ID column (such as `doc_id` or `sample_id`) is still worth keeping: it is copied to the output, it lets you inspect individual disagreements, and Lab's [human reliability](human-reliability.qmd) tools require one.

## Bundled Example Tasks

The package ships with example tasks so you can test the workflow immediately:

```python
from codebook_lab import copy_example_task, list_example_tasks

print(list_example_tasks())
copy_example_task("policy-sentiment", "./my_tasks", overwrite=True)
```

Then point an experiment at the folder that contains your task folders:

```python
from codebook_lab import ExperimentSpec, run_experiment

result = run_experiment(
    ExperimentSpec(
        task="policy-sentiment",
        model="gemma3:270m",
        country_iso_code="IRL",
    ),
    task_root="my_tasks",
)
```

Lab looks for a task in `task_root` first. If it isn't there, Lab falls back to a bundled example task with the same name, if one exists. So a mistyped `task_root` with `task="policy-sentiment"` silently runs the bundled copy instead of yours. The `codebook_path` column of the [runs table](outputs-metrics.qmd#tidy-metrics-tables) shows which copy each run used.

## Custom Task Checklist

Before running a custom task, check:

- the codebook has a valid `text_column`
- the CSV contains that text column
- every human label column matches the codebook-derived column name
- checkbox values are stored as `0` or `1`
- dropdown values match one of the allowed options
- Likert values are inside the configured numeric range
- span values are JSON lists of `start`, `end`, `text`, and optional `label` objects
- conditional child fields are blank when the parent condition is not satisfied
- a parent question comes before any question that depends on it
- rows are in the same order you will score them in, ideally with an ID column
